before: A galvanic (fuel) cell consumes O₂ at a lead anode (Pb + 2OH⁻ → PbO + H₂O + 2e⁻), generating a current proportional to O₂ partial pressure at the gold cathode (O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻).
after: In a lead/gold galvanic (fuel) oxygen cell, oxygen is reduced at the gold cathode (O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻), while lead is oxidised at the anode (Pb + 2OH⁻ → PbO + H₂O + 2e⁻). The resulting current is proportional to O₂ partial pressure.

before: Free radicals have unpaired electrons — superoxide, hydroxyl radical, peroxynitrite", cites: ["Wright 1999 (MetHb)"]
after: Free radicals have unpaired electrons: superoxide, hydroxyl radical and nitric oxide. Hydrogen peroxide and peroxynitrite are nonradical oxidants; ONOO⁻ is a reactive nitrogen species", cites: ["Pacher 2007 Peroxynitrite"]

before: Free radicals contain an unpaired electron and are highly reactive. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) include superoxide (O₂⁻·), hydroxyl radical (OH·) and peroxynitrite (ONOO⁻).
after: Free radicals contain an unpaired electron: examples are superoxide (O₂⁻·), hydroxyl radical (OH·) and nitric oxide (NO·). Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) is a nonradical reactive oxygen species; peroxynitrite (ONOO⁻) is a nonradical reactive nitrogen species, although its reactions can generate radicals.

before: Pb + 2OH⁻ → PbO + H₂O + 2e⁻; at the cathode, O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻.
after: Pb + 2OH⁻ → PbO + H₂O + 2e⁻ (lead oxidation); at the cathode, O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻ (oxygen reduction). <InlineRef topicId="oxidation-reduction" refLabel="Cross & Plunkett Ch.3" />
